Capturing it and filing it as before/ would have produced images that are pre-change in name only. 2ec8788 is the last commit before the first implementation commit, so it is the true pre-change tree. seed_rationale: The skill's dependable default (one reachable site, one .invalid that never resolves so Down renders without waiting on a real outage) plus a third unlabelled site, because render.ts shows label-or-URL per row and the feature's evidence is about which rows exist. method_override is omitted deliberately: model.rs marks it #[serde(default)], so the seed parses without it. Every run — the before pass and both after passes — used this list verbatim from the manifest, which is what makes them comparable.

views.why: The populated list plus the add form. Reference for FR-009/FR-012 and SC-003 — after the change, a refused add must produce zero rows, so the after run compares row-for-row against this.
views.how_to_reach: Launch with the seed above; wait ~10s for Pending to resolve to Up/Down.
views.before_observation: All three seed rows render with resolved statuses — Example: Up, Never Up: Down, https://example.org: Up. The unlabelled third site falls back to its URL as the row title. At 480x320 the Add button wraps below the input row and the 'Launch at login' footer clips at the window floor. Every one of these traits is already present before the change, which is what makes them pre-existing layout rather than something this feature introduced.
views.after_observation: Identical in every structural respect: three rows, Example: Up, Never Up: Down, https://example.org: Up, the unlabelled site still falling back to its URL as the row title. At 480x320 the Add button still wraps below the input row and the footer still clips at the window floor — pre-existing minimum-size layout, not a regression. Outside the wall-clock 'LAST CHECKED' text the two captures differ by ~175 pixels out of 345,600 (0.05%), all of it title-glyph antialiasing and two footer-checkbox pixels; see comparison.per_view_breakdown.

The narrow pair is bit-for-bit identical (0 differing pixels) and the default pair differs by 4 pixels in the 'Launch at login' checkbox. This is store.rs's load-failure message, not FR-004's poison-recovery message — the latter needs a genuinely poisoned lock, which no sequence of clicks can produce. What the shot demonstrates is the mechanism FR-004 reuses: same #banner element, same placement, same styling, so the poison warning surfaces here rather than through anything new.

comparison.method: Per-pixel RGB comparison of each before/after pair at tolerance 12/255, from a compiled Swift helper reading the original PNGs. Reported as a total count plus a distribution over 20px row bands and 40px column bands, so each difference can be attributed to a screen region instead of inferred from a bounding box. (An earlier bounding-box-only summary was misleading: a handful of outlying pixels stretched the box across the whole window and made the change look larger than it was.)

per_view_breakdown.window title glyphs (y0-19, x80-199): 169-172 px in each of the four non-banner pairs, and ZERO in both banner pairs. Cropping and magnifying the region 4x shows the same string 'Site Checker' at the same position in both runs, differing only in antialiasing weight. The banner pairs scoring zero in exactly this region is the control that proves the title itself did not change.
per_view_breakdown.LAST CHECKED column (x360-399 default /: 274-322 px. Relative-time text ('38s ago' vs '42s ago'), wall-clock dependent and impossible to match across two runs taken ~30 minutes apart.
per_view_breakdown.add-error input row + error line (y220-2: 34 px default, 66 px narrow, add-error pairs only. The text caret sits at a different offset: the before pass clicked into the middle of 'ftp://example.com' so its caret renders mid-string, while this pass appended to the end. Same field contents, same error string, different caret position.
per_view_breakdown.footer checkbox (y440-479 default / y300: 0-4 px of 'Launch at login' checkbox antialiasing.

comparison.interpretation: Nothing structural changed. Every differing pixel falls into one of four buckets — title-glyph antialiasing, the wall-clock relative-time text, the text caret's resting position in the add form, and a few checkbox antialiasing pixels — and none of them is content. The strongest single piece of evidence is warning-banner-narrow at 0 differing pixels: the banner mechanism FR-004 reuses renders bit-for-bit identically before and after. No row, column, control, label, status dot, or error string moved or changed. That is the expected result: plan.md said zero frontend files change, and baseline_source.frontend_identity_check proves it independently.

ui_relevance.reasoning: plan.md states zero frontend files change and src/ is untouched. But the skill's exception for backend work that changes user-visible output applies: FR-004 adds a new store-warning banner message, FR-010 rewords the refused-add message the user reads (it must stop implying the change is merely unsaved), and FR-009 removes a row that appears today. Those are user-visible output changes, so this was NOT treated as a skip.

before_rerun_declined.invocation: mode: before, target branch: main — unattended re-invocation of the same skill on the same resolved FEATURE_DIR
before_rerun_declined.action_taken: NONE. No pnpm install, no build, no app launch, no seed write, no capture. Not one byte of before/ or after/ was touched; this manifest entry is the only change.
before_rerun_declined.why: The resolved feature is already shipped. Its three implementation commits (f086cfa, 7ea3e66, 8feb989) and its spec commit (2ec8788) are all ancestors of HEAD; HEAD = origin/main = 42f44ca; the working tree is clean; and specs/ contains no directory newer than this one. There is therefore no pending implementation for a baseline to precede — a "before" run has nothing to be before.
before_rerun_declined.what_capturing_would_have_done: One of two bad outcomes, both destructive. (a) Take the instruction "target branch: main" literally and capture main tip into before/ — that is the documented silent-corruption mode: images that are pre-change in name only, which would make the before/after diff read as falsely identical. (b) Rebuild 2ec8788 and re-shoot the baseline — redundant, and it would overwrite six verified PNGs with new ones differing only in wall-clock relative-time text and capture conditions, invalidating the per-pixel numbers already published in comparison.results and embedded in PR #5.
before_rerun_declined.capture_not_blocked_note: Recorded explicitly so this no-op is not misread as a repeat of before_run_blocked_attempt. Capture was fully available at decision time and was declined on scope grounds. Note the display geometry differs from earlier runs (2880x1800 here vs 5120x1440 during the after pass) — another reason a re-shot baseline would not be comparable to the committed one.
before_rerun_declined.base_branch_health: Not exercised. The unattended instruction to report a broken base branch does not apply: nothing was built or started this run. The last actual evidence stands — the base tree (2ec8788) compiled and launched twice in before_run, and main compiled and launched three times in after_run, with no build failure or startup panic.
before_rerun_declined.user_data: Untouched, and verified rather than assumed. sites.json holds the user's 5 real sites and is byte-identical to /tmp/site-checker-sites-SAFETY-COPY.json; no sites.json.shots-backup exists, so no earlier run leaked; port 1420 is free and no site-checker or vite process is running. Because nothing was seeded, the step-3 backup was never created and the step-7 restore was never needed.
before_rerun_declined.skipped_md_deliberately_not_written: SKIPPED.md means "this feature has no UI surface". That is false here — ui_relevance.verdict is ui-relevant and six real images exist. Writing it would also poison a future `after` run, which treats SKIPPED.md as a prediction to verify and would then skip a feature that genuinely has captured UI evidence.

The committed pair is 1x: 720x480 and 480x320, captured on the 5120x1440 physical display in use from 14:25 to 15:12. Today's session runs on a 'Screen Sharing Virtual Display' — 2880x1800 physical for 1440x900 points, a 2x backing scale. Two independent probes confirm the consequence: screencapture -R 100,100,720,480 returned a 1440x960 PNG, and a live grab of the real 720x480 app window also returned 1440x960. A re-shot after/ would therefore be 1440x960 and 960x640, and could not be per-pixel compared against a 720x480 and 480x320 before/.

They could not be recomputed at the new scale without also re-shooting before/, which would mean rebuilding 2ec8788 and discarding the verified baseline as well. Net effect: verified evidence destroyed, zero content gained, because the subject tree is identical.
why_no_recapture.instruction_read: The invocation asked to reuse the before pass's manifest so the pair is comparable. Honouring that intent is exactly what forbids a re-shoot here: on this display the new images could not be comparable to the baseline, so re-capturing would defeat the stated reason for reusing the manifest rather than serve it.

notes: This after pass is a RE-RUN that replaces all six images committed in 74cb8db. The reason is capture conditions, not code: the tree is byte-identical between the two passes (see environment.after_run_superseded.tree_identity), but the original set was taken before any baseline existed and one shot caught an inactive window. Re-taking them under the before pass's conditions cut the largest pair diff from 0.62% to 0.13% and made warning-banner-narrow bit-for-bit identical.

Both branches build and start cleanly. The unattended-run instruction about reporting a broken app does not apply: the app compiled and launched three times in this pass without error, and the base branch compiled and launched twice in the before pass.

This session's desktop aggressively stole keyboard focus between agent tool calls — Firefox, VS Code and Zoom each took frontmost at different points, and the app window also moved from 2200,263 to 1937,152 partway through. The first attempts at the add-error view failed because of this: synthetic clicks aimed at the window's old coordinates landed elsewhere, and one of them left the URL field reading 'ftp://example.co' after a trailing backspace event arrived out of order and ate the final character. The fix was a new single-process helper (/tmp/seq-helper, built outside the checkout) that re-asserts AXFrontmost immediately before every click, keystroke and capture, and records the frontmost process at the moment of each grab; every kept image was captured with frontmost_at_capture=site-checker. The corrupted field was caught by cropping and magnifying the input 4x rather than trusting the full-size render, and the view was re-shot correctly.

CAVEAT worth flagging: during the focus-recovery attempts, roughly a dozen synthetic single left-clicks were posted at fixed screen coordinates that — because the app window had moved — may have landed on whatever window was on top at that point, including the user's Zoom and VS Code windows. They were plain single clicks with no drag and no typing, so the risk is low, but it is not zero and is recorded here rather than omitted.

The duplicate-id refusal (FR-010) and the poison-recovery warning (FR-004) are still not reachable by clicking on either branch — every add mints a fresh id, and no sequence of clicks poisons a lock. Those two strings remain covered by the automated tests, not by these images.

The user's real sites.json was moved to sites.json.shots-backup and additionally copied out of tree to /tmp/site-checker-sites-SAFETY-after-run-20260806-1455.json before seeding. It was restored at the end and verified three ways: sha1 7150bef89871c83ceb3b9064e67b8ac1e499ee56 (unchanged), a full diff against the safety copy (clean), and confirmation that no .shots-backup file was left behind. Each dev process tree was launched into its own process group (perl setpgrp) and torn down with kill -TERM then -KILL on the group; after every teardown no site-checker, tauri or vite process survived and port 1420 was confirmed free.

Nothing outside FEATURE_DIR/screenshots/ was modified in the repo. Dev-server logs went to /tmp/tauri-dev-after*.log and the capture helpers to /tmp, both outside the checkout, so neither could be picked up by the git auto-commit hooks.

tasks.md still has T025 and T040 marked incomplete ('click-through NOT performed'). This run exercised more of them — the app launched three times, the list loaded, checks ran, an add was attempted and correctly refused, and sites.json came back byte-identical — but the delete and edit click-throughs were still not exercised, and this command does not modify feature artifacts other than screenshots/.

A second `before` invocation arrived on 2026-08-06 ~17:44, after the feature had already merged to main (PR #5) with a complete, per-pixel-diffed before/after pair. It was declined as a no-op and no images were written — see environment.before_rerun_declined for the full reasoning, the preflight showing capture was available (not blocked), and the verification that the user data file was never touched. The short version: the feature is shipped, so there is no pending change for a baseline to precede, and either way of "capturing" would have destroyed verified evidence rather than adding any.

A second `after` invocation arrived on 2026-08-06 ~18:22 and was likewise declined as a no-op — see environment.after_rerun_declined. Unlike the before re-run, an after re-run is not semantically wrong (main's tip IS the after state), so it was assessed on its merits and refused for a different, measurable reason: this session's display has a 2x backing scale, so a re-shot after/ would be 1440x960 while the committed before/ is 720x480. The two sets could not be per-pixel compared, and the comparison numbers already published in PR #5 would be destroyed to gain nothing — the app tree is byte-identical to the one after/ was shot from. What this run DID add is fresh liveness evidence: the app was built and launched once on HEAD (3e9972c) and rendered the user's real five-site list with every site Up and no panic, so the unattended brief's 'report a broken app' branch is answered with a live result rather than an inherited claim.

The 2x scale finding is worth carrying forward: any future screenshot pass for this repo should record the display's backing scale alongside the window size, because a pair captured across a scale change is not comparable no matter how carefully the window is sized. The committed sets here are all 1x.
